column1: # The adjective sense judge on the gloss heuristic's proposals (D97 decision 7, revised 2026-10-01) — DRAFT
# for the owner's review: a fixed sample of 30 of the 820 senses it accepts at 0.85 on lemmas no source
# attests. Review: correct | wrong | unclear, with a note.
# lemma <TAB> preposition <TAB> offset <TAB> confidence <TAB> review <TAB> note <TAB> gloss

column7: exhibiting equivalence or correspondence among constituents of an entity or between different entities

column6: «eyes moist with tears»
column7: slightly wet; "clothes damp with perspiration"; "a moist breeze"; "eyes moist with tears"

column6: a duration adjunct: «hitless for three innings»
column7: (of a batter) without a hit; "he went hitless for three innings"

column6: «woven into a whole»
column7: made or constructed by interlacing threads or strips of material or other elements into a whole; "woven fabrics"; "woven baskets"; "the incidents woven into the story"; "folk songs woven into a symphony"
not burdened with difficulties or responsibilities; "unburdened by an overarching theory"- Alex Inkeles

column6: a place adjunct: «flabby around the middle»
column7: out of condition; not strong or robust; incapable of exertion or endurance; "he was too soft for the army"; "flabby around the middle"; "flaccid cheeks"

column6: a to-infinitive, not to + NP: «obligated to repay»
column7: caused by law or conscience to follow a certain course; "felt obligated to repay the kindness"; "was obligated to pay off the student loan"

column6: «dabbled with moonlight»
column7: covered with bright patches (often used in combination); "waves dabbled with moonlight"; "a blood-spattered room"; "gardens splashed with color"; "kitchen walls splattered with grease"
packed full to capacity; "chowder chockablock with pieces of fish"

column6: `by` measures the margin («down by a run»), which D95's `by` over a value reads
column7: being or moving lower in position or less in some value; "lay face down"; "the moon is down"; "our team is down by a run"; "down by a pawn"; "the stock market is down today"
aware of yourself as an individual or of your own being and actions and thoughts; "self-conscious awareness"; "self-conscious about their roles as guardians of the social values"- D.M.Potter

column6: the gloss quotes «careful with money»
column7: mindful of the future in spending money; "careful with money"

not representative of a group, class, or type; "a group that is atypical of the target audience"; "a class of atypical mosses"; "atypical behavior is not the accepted type of response that we expect from children"

column6: «untrue to her husband»
column7: (used especially of persons) not dependable in devotion or affection; unfaithful; "a false friend"; "when lovers prove untrue"

column6: a to-infinitive, not to + NP: «certain to fail»
column7: certain to occur; destined or inevitable; "he was certain to fail"; "his fate is certain"; "In this life nothing is certain but death and taxes"- Benjamin Franklin; "he faced certain death"; "sudden but sure regret"; "he is sure to win"

column6: the gloss quotes «on guard against con artists»
column7: vigilant; "on guard against con artists"; "must remain on your guard in such a situation"

column6: an adjunct
column7: not capable of being carried out or put into practice; "refloating the sunken ship proved impracticable because of its fragility"; "a suggested reform that was unfeasible in the prevailing circumstances"

column6: the gloss quotes «laid up with a bad cold»
column7: ill and usually confined; "laid up with a bad cold"

column6: a direction adjunct: «hair combed to the side»
column7: (of hair) made tidy with a comb; "with hair combed to the side"

filled with the emotional impact of overwhelming surprise or shock; "an amazed audience gave the magician a standing ovation"; "I stood enthralled, astonished by the vastness and majesty of the cathedral"; "astounded viewers wept at the pictures from the Oklahoma City bombing"; "stood in stunned silence"; "stunned scientists found not one but at least three viruses"

column6: «correct in his judgment»
column7: correct in opinion or judgment; "time proved him right"

column6: the gloss quotes «acceptive of every new idea»
column7: accepting willingly; "acceptive of every new idea"; "an acceptant type of mind"

column6: «acceptable for publication»
column7: meeting requirements; "the step makes a satisfactory seat"

column6: the gloss quotes «accessible to the nonprofessional reader»
column7: capable of being read with comprehension; "readily accessible to the nonprofessional reader"; "the tales seem more approachable than his more difficult novels"

column6: «certain of success»
column7: having or feeling no doubt or uncertainty; confident and assured; "felt certain of success"; "was sure (or certain) she had seen it"; "was very sure in his beliefs"; "sure of her friends"

column6: «fringed by an industrial belt»
column7: surrounded as with a border or fringe; sometimes used in combination; "a large suburban community...fringed by an industrial area"; "a grass-fringed stream"

column6: the by-phrase is the passive verb's: «knocked silly by the impact»
column7: dazed from or as if from repeated blows; "knocked silly by the impact"; "slaphappy with exhaustion"

column6: «low in fat»
column7: less than normal in degree or intensity or amount; "low prices"; "the reservoir is low"

column6: a setting, «permissible in cosmology», not a complement
column7: that may be accepted or conceded; "a kind of speculation that was permissible in cosmology but inadmissible in medicine"
having ones attention or mind or energy engaged; "she keeps herself fully occupied with volunteer activities"; "deeply engaged in conversation"
